title: イングリッシュマスター  (An English Master)

segments.t: One wrong word nearly got Muranishi thrown out of Nakai's mansion, so he thinks fast. He promises Nakai that practicing a handful of cheerful English words will make him an instant hit abroad—and soon both men are shouting at the top of their lungs. Listen to Muranishi close his very first sale.
めっそうもございません！お薦めする理由がもう一つあります。
何だ？
愛のコミュニケーションを取ることができます。
ここに書かれている言葉を覚えて使えば大丈夫です。
例えば？
シンプルに、オー、グッド、グッド！
それだったら俺も言えるぜ。グッド！
パーフェクトでございます！
ハロー！ラブ！グッド！
あんたたち！
奥様、明日からご主人はイングリッシュマスターになります。
買ってもいい？
From panicked humility to triumphant applause, Muranishi rides every emotional wave in Japanese. Let's look at the key expressions.
めっそうもございません！
'Perish the thought!' Built around humble "messou", this old-fashioned set expression waves away an accusation—'heaven forbid, I would never dream of looking down on you!'
お薦めする理由がもう一つあります。
'There is one more reason I recommend this.' "Osusume" means recommendation—the word printed on every restaurant menu's chef specials! "Mou hitotsu" adds 'one more'.
ここに書かれている言葉を覚えて使えば大丈夫です。

'If you learn and use the words written here, you are all set.' "Koko ni kakarete iru" describes words 'written here'. Linking "oboete", memorize, to "tsukaeba", if you use, leads smoothly into reassuring "daijoubu desu".
例えば？
'For example?' One word, "tatoeba", works both to introduce your own example and, with a rising voice, to ask someone 'such as?'
それだったら俺も言えるぜ。
'If that is all, I can say it too.' "Sore dattara" means 'if it is just that'. Turning "iu", to say, into "ieru" builds 'can say', and masculine "ze" adds swagger.
パーフェクトでございます！
'That is absolute perfection!' Muranishi dresses up English 'perfect'—"paafekuto"—with grand "de gozaimasu", cheering his customer like a prize pupil.
あんたたち！
'Hey, you two!' Hearing the commotion, Nakai's wife bursts in shouting "antatachi", built from casual "anta", you, plus group-marker "tachi".
奥様、明日からご主人はイングリッシュマスターになります。
'Madam, starting tomorrow your husband becomes an English master.' Notice the respectful pair for someone else's marriage: "okusama" addresses a wife politely, while "goshujin" refers to her husband.
買ってもいい？

'Can I buy it?' After acting like a tough boss all afternoon, Nakai meekly asks his wife "katte mo ii", literally 'is buying okay?'—the everyday pattern with "mo ii" for asking permission! Now let's listen to Muranishi's first victorious sale from start to finish.

愛のコミュニケーションを取ることができます。
ここに書かれている言葉を覚えて使えば大丈夫です。
例えば？
シンプルに、オー、グッド、グッド！
それだったら俺も言えるぜ。グッド！
パーフェクトでございます！
ハロー！ラブ！グッド！
あんたたち！
奥様、明日からご主人はイングリッシュマスターになります。
買ってもいい？
Take away "osusume" for recommendations, "tatoeba" for 'for example', and "katte mo ii" whenever you want to ask if it is okay to buy something. See you in scene fifteen.
ありがとうございます、また会いましょう。
